title: What Is Computation
summary: The four pillars of computational thinking — decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithm design — and why they're a way of thinking, not a way of coding.

references.label: Wing, "Computational Thinking" — Communications of the ACM (2006)
ISTE/CSTA Operational Definition of Computational Thinking

title: Problem Decomposition and Algorithmic Thinking
summary: Breaking a problem into an ordered sequence of unambiguous steps before writing a single line of real code, using a toy grid-world/robot example to separate algorithmic thinking from syntax.

references.label: Wing, "Computational Thinking" — Communications of the ACM (2006)

title: Variables and Primitive Types
summary: Naming a piece of memory to hold a value, and the primitive types (int, float, bool, str) every program is built from.

references.label: Python Tutorial — An Informal Introduction to Python

title: Expressions and Assignment
summary: Combining values and operators into expressions, and the difference between mathematical equality and assignment's 'store the result here'.

references.label: Python Tutorial — An Informal Introduction to Python

title: Input and Output
summary: Reading a value from the user and printing a result back — the smallest possible feedback loop a program can have.

title: Conditional Control Flow
summary: Branching a program's execution with if/elif/else based on a boolean condition.

references.label: Python Tutorial — More Control Flow Tools

title: Iteration and Loops
summary: Repeating a block of code with while and for, and the loop invariants that keep a repeated computation correct.

references.label: Python Tutorial — More Control Flow Tools

title: Floating-Point and Approximation
summary: Why floating-point numbers are an approximation of the reals, not the reals themselves, and what that means for equality checks and accumulated error.

title: Guess-and-Check and Bisection Search
summary: Solving equations no closed form covers by successive approximation — exhaustive guess-and-check first, then bisection search cutting the search space in half each step.

title: Decomposition and Abstraction via Functions
summary: Wrapping a block of logic behind a name so a caller can use it without knowing how it works inside — the mechanism behind computational thinking's abstraction pillar.

references.label: Wing, "Computational Thinking" — Communications of the ACM (2006)
ACM/IEEE CS2013 — Software Development Fundamentals KA

title: Parameters and Return Values
summary: Passing data into a function and getting a result back out — parameter binding, default values, and what a function returns when it doesn't say.

references.label: Python Tutorial — More Control Flow Tools

title: Functions as First-Class Objects
summary: Treating a function itself as a value — assigning it to a variable, passing it as an argument, or writing one inline as a lambda.

references.label: Python Tutorial — More Control Flow Tools

title: Lists and Mutability
summary: Storing an ordered, growable sequence of values in a list, and the difference between a mutable list and an immutable value like a number or string.

title: Aliasing and Cloning
summary: Two variables can point at the same mutable list in memory — mutating through one changes what the other sees, unless you clone instead of alias.

title: Tuples
summary: An immutable, fixed-size sequence — when to reach for a tuple instead of a list, and how tuple unpacking reads cleaner than manual indexing.

title: Dictionaries
summary: Storing key-value pairs for near-constant-time lookup by key instead of by position, backed by a hash table.

title: Testing and Debugging
summary: Writing test cases before you trust a function, and a systematic process for isolating a bug instead of guessing at print statements.

references.label: ACM/IEEE CS2013 — Software Development Fundamentals KA

title: Exceptions and Assertions
summary: Raising and catching exceptions for conditions a caller must handle, and assertions for conditions that should never happen at all.

title: Recursion
summary: A function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem, bottoming out at a base case.

title: Recursion on Structural Data
summary: Applying recursion to a value's shape — walking a nested list or a string letter-by-letter — rather than to a shrinking number.

title: Timing and Counting Operations
summary: Measuring how a program's actual running time grows as its input grows, by timing it and by counting its operations.

title: Big-O and Asymptotic Complexity
summary: Describing an algorithm's growth rate independent of any specific machine, using Big-O to bound its worst case.

references.label: ACM/IEEE CS2013 — Software Development Fundamentals KA

title: Sorting Algorithms: An Introduction
summary: A first pass at sorting: comparing simple quadratic sorts (bubble/selection/insertion) against a divide-and-conquer sort (merge sort), and why the comparison matters once Big-O is on the table.
